Washington has long accused China of subsidizing industry and flooding global markets with low-cost exports ranging from steel to electric vehicles and solar products.

Beijing earlier reiterated its opposition to “trade wars” and rejected allegations of overcapacity, but stopped short of threatening retaliation.

‘FALSE ISSUE,’ CHINA SAYS

“The so-called ‘overcapacity’ is a false issue, and China opposes using it as an excuse for political manipulation,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said, urging the world’s top two economies to maintain stable relations.

The USTR also proposed capped tariff rates of 18% for imported goods from Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Bangladesh, and 15%, including existing “Most Favored Nation” duties, for Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, the EU and Switzerland.

India, which has yet to reach a trade deal with the Trump administration, would face a 17% tariff rate if an agreement is finalized and a 25% rate if talks fail, the USTR said. Singapore would receive a capped tariff rate of 10%.

Greer told CNBC the proposed caps were consistent with trade agreements reached over the past year that also lowered barriers to US exports.

“We’re sticking to that in terms of our proposals because we think a lot of these deals we made actually solve a lot of the problems we see in excess capacity or can go toward it,” Greer said. “So you know we’ve talked to our trading partners about this. They know what we’re proposing. I think a lot of this is baked in.”

Mexico and Norway were excluded from the proposals because investigations into their trade practices remain under way, Greer said.

Even so, the prospect of new trade barriers weighed on stock markets on Wednesday amid a renewed selloff in tech stocks. Major US indexes opened down more than 1%, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite .IXIC down more than 3%.

“It is another reminder that while the legal justification for tariffs keeps changing, US protectionism is becoming increasingly difficult to unwind,” ING analysts wrote.

NEW DUTIES WON’T EXCEED NEGOTIATED LIMITS

Trump’s tariffs have contributed to higher prices for US consumers, and a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll conducted after Republicans’ midterm losses found 62% of respondents supported efforts to repeal them.

But Trump has long vowed to restore duties struck down by the US Supreme Court in February. The latest measures follow an eight-month investigation into unfair trade practices under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

Greer said the proposed tariffs would not apply to about $30 billion of Chinese imports under consideration for tariff reductions through a bilateral mechanism known as the Board of Trade.

However, the new duties would be added to tariffs imposed on Chinese goods during Trump’s first term, which total roughly 25%.

They would not be imposed on top of the 10% and 12.5% tariffs introduced in July on a broader group of 60 trading partners over allegations of lax enforcement of anti-forced-labor laws.

น่าน.title: Rajadamnern Stadium to open billion-baht world-class Muay Thai venue in Phuket
น่าน.summary:
Central Pattana and Global Sport Ventures plan to open a Muay Thai stadium at Central Phuket in early 2029, bringing Bangkok’s Rajadamnern Stadium brand outside the capital for the first time. The project represents an investment of more than 1 billion baht.

Rajadamnern Stadium Phuket will cover 9,000 square metres and accommodate about 2,500 spectators. The companies said it would be Thailand’s largest combat sports stadium. It will host live bouts and shows exploring Muay Thai traditions, and will house a Muay Thai museum, restaurants, cafés and bars.
The stadium will anchor Central Pattana’s 14-rai expansion of Central Phuket, a shopping and mixed-use development that the company values at more than 26 billion baht. Central Pattana also plans to double the size of the mall’s luxury retail zone, with Cartier set to open a store there in 2027.

The mall is also expanding its dining offering. Andaman Table, a 3,700-square-metre dining area scheduled to open on 1 December, will bring together more than 90 eateries, including Phuket establishments Mee Ton Poe, Moo Krob Jee Hong and Nai Mueang.
Global Sport Ventures operates Bangkok’s Rajadamnern Stadium and runs the Rajadamnern World Series. Thainchai Pisitwuttinan, chief executive of the series, said Phuket’s popularity as a Muay Thai training destination helped drive the decision to open a venue on the island. The company aims to attract one million international visitors to the stadium each year.

Architecture firms Populous, whose projects include London’s Wembley Stadium, and Nikken Sekkei, which has worked on the redevelopment of Barcelona’s Camp Nou, are involved in the design.
Phuket welcomed more than 10.25 million visitors in the first nine months of 2026, 74% of them from overseas, according to figures cited by the companies.

น่าน.title: Thailand Lawmakers Pass Clean Air Bill in Unanimous Vote
น่าน.summary:
BANGKOK — Thailand’s House of Representatives unanimously approved the revised Clean Air Management Bill on Nov. 25, sending the long-awaited legislation to the Senate for a final confirmation vote scheduled for Nov. 30. Lawmakers voted 430-0 in favor of the compromise text, advancing a seven-year legislative push to curb hazardous fine particulate pollution before peak haze conditions return.

The measure establishes a statutory right to clean air and equips provincial officials with direct enforcement powers against industrial and agricultural polluters. If the Senate endorses the draft next week, the bill will proceed to royal endorsement and publication in the Royal Gazette before taking legal effect.

• Thailand’s House voted 430-0 on Nov. 25 to approve the compromise Clean Air Management Bill after reconciling 92 Senate-amended sections.

• The draft legislation empowers provincial governors to regulate polluters, establishes a dedicated Clean Air Fund and authorizes cross-border diplomatic action.

A joint parliamentary committee chaired by Bhumjaithai Party lawmaker Anurak Chureemas reconciled differences between the two chambers across 11 meetings, accepting 54 of the Senate’s 92 amendments while refining 50 sections. The committee retained core economic instruments built around the polluter-pays principle alongside a dedicated Clean Air Fund to finance mitigation projects.

Under the revised framework, provincial governors will chair local clean air committees, with provincial administrative organization chiefs serving as vice chairs. These panels gain authority to order polluting facilities to halt operations, restrict open agricultural burning and require public disclosure through a Pollutant Release and Transfer Register.

Debate before the vote highlighted sharp adjustments to financial penalties during upper-house review. People’s Party lawmaker Phattharaphong Leelaphatreported that maximum fines for certain pollution offenses were lowered from 50 million baht in the House’s initial draft to 5 million baht in the compromise version.

Beyond factory smokestacks, the bill codifies protections for vulnerable populations, including children, pregnant women, outdoor workers and low-income residents exposed to seasonal smog. It mandates local air quality warning systems and requires state agencies to integrate health impact assessments into regional haze response plans.

The text also addresses smoke drifting across national borders. It assigns the Ministry of Foreign Affairs a formal mandate to coordinate with neighboring governments alongside the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment, creating legal backing for regional crop traceability and supply-chain accountability.

The push for binding air quality rules gained urgency from recurring public health emergencies across northern Thailand, where winter temperature inversions trap smoke inside mountain basins between February and April. In upper northern provinces such as Chiang Rai and Chiang Mai, fine dust readings routinely breach national safety thresholds, straining hospital respiratory wards and disrupting winter tourism.

Past governments relied on temporary provincial burning bans and cabinet resolutions that lacked unified statutory teeth across ministries. Citizen networks first submitted a people’s version of the clean air legislation more than seven years ago, only to see earlier drafts stall across parliamentary dissolutions and committee reviews.

น่าน.title: Bangkok Chao Phraya Dinner Cruises: Prices and Tips
น่าน.summary:
Bangkok’s riverside temples and landmarks take on a different look after dark, making a Chao Phraya dinner cruise an easy way to see the city from the water. Options range from casual buffet boats with live entertainment to premium experiences aboard restored rice barges, such as Anantara Riverside’s restored-rice-barge dinner cruise.

Prices vary widely, and the lowest headline fare may not include drinks or other extras. This guide compares cruise styles, November 2026 price ranges, and the booking details that can affect your evening, including the pier, schedule, and ticket inclusions.

Most Bangkok dinner cruises spend about two hours on the Chao Phraya River, combining an evening meal with views of the city’s riverfront. Depending on the boat and direction of travel, passengers may see Wat Arun, the Grand Palace area, and Rama VIII Bridge. The route, visibility, meal, and entertainment vary by operator, and weather can affect the views from open decks.

A buffet ticket usually includes a mix of Thai and international dishes, with menus varying by cruise. Some boats add seafood, such as prawns or other seafood selections, while live music and Thai dance performances may be part of the evening. Large vessels often have several decks, including open-air areas where guests can watch the riverfront pass by.

That lively setup suits travelers who enjoy a broad menu and shared entertainment. For a look at the riverside landmarks along Bangkok’s boat routes, remember that a dinner cruise offers passing views rather than time ashore at each site. Boats may pass Wat Arun and the Grand Palace area before continuing toward Rama VIII Bridge; one cruise operator’s route highlights also include these landmarks.

Check the ticket details before booking, especially for drinks. Some packages include selected beverages, but others charge separately for beer, wine, or soft drinks. A seafood buffet or free-flow offer may also apply only to a specific ticket tier, so compare the inclusions for your sailing rather than relying on a general description.

Manohra offers a different pace aboard a restored rice barge, with a Thai set menu and a smaller-scale feel than a large buffet boat. It lists three two-hour dinner rounds, departing at 6:00, 7:00, and 8:30 p.m. That range can help guests choose an earlier meal or a later evening on the river.

The higher price reflects the set-menu format and boat experience, but it doesn’t automatically include alcoholic drinks. Manohra’s listed packages distinguish between free-flow soft drinks and options that include wine and beer. Check the current menu and package terms before booking, since inclusions can differ even within the same operator.

Neither style suits every traveler. A buffet cruise brings more food choices and a livelier deck, while a set-menu barge offers a more measured dinner with fewer guests around. Compare the meal format, drink allowance, sailing time, and expected atmosphere to find the ticket that fits your evening.

In November 2026, Chao Phraya dinner cruises range from about THB 900 for a budget buffet ticket to more than THB 5,000 per person for a premium set menu with drinks. Treat these figures as a price snapshot, not guaranteed fares: the amount can change by sailing date, seller, guest category, and package inclusions.

น่าน.title: Man United denied at Sporting as referee overshadows Fernandes double
น่าน.summary:
Mauricio Pochettino must wait for his first win as Manchester United coach, after a wild 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, with the hosts equalising thanks to a goalkeeping error from Senne Lammens.

The Belgian stopper’s poor handling allowed Luis Suarez to complete a brace for the hosts, cancelling out United playmaker Bruno Fernandes’s double against his former side.

United gave away two penalties in the first half, the second converted by Suarez, before Fernandes equalised from the spot early in the second half.

Fernandes sent United ahead with a lucky bounce taking his effort over the Sporting goalkeeper, before Suarez’s acrobatic effort levelled the game.

United midfielder Youri Tielemans was sent off in stoppage time for a second yellow card to end a compelling and often erratic match.

A crushing 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool in the Premier League at the weekend, leaving United 19th, was a disastrous first game at the helm for Pochettino after replacing Michael Carrick.

Pochettino brought Harry Maguire into the three-man defence as he shuffled his pack, as well as starting Joshua Zirkzee in place of the suspended Matheus Cunha.

Neither side took many risks in the opening stages, with few chances of note until the game burst into life midway through the first half as United lost control.

Lisandro Martinez brought down Geny Catamo in the area and Sporting were awarded a penalty.

The hosts blew their chance from the spot, with Suarez’s scuffed effort easily saved by Lammens, but the Red Devils gave away another spot kick just a couple of minutes later.

Goalkeeper Lammens came flying off his line and clattered Maxi Araujo, and this time Colombian striker Suarez made no mistake from the spot.

United thought they had equalised when Amad Diallo hit the crossbar and then nodded home the rebound, but the goal was disallowed to their dismay.

Youri Tielemans was ruled to have fouled Goncalo Inacio, although he seemed to win the ball, upsetting United further after Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool on Sunday that was later rescinded.

Fernandes pulled United level early in the second half from the spot after Eduardo Quaresma brought down Martinez.

The former Sporting playmaker calmly stroked his penalty beyond the dive of Kaique Pereira into the bottom left corner.

Fernandes said on the eve of the game he had stopped contract talks because he wanted to focus on helping United improve their form after a dire start to the season.

The midfielder soon had his second goal, with the help of a bizarre bounce off a divot on the pitch.

Fernandes’s low effort from distance seemed bound for Pereira’s hands, but suddenly bounced up off a patch of uneven turf and fortuitously over the goalkeeper’s head.

The Portugal international bent a free-kick narrowly off target as he looked to complete his hat-trick.

Lammens saved well from Sergi Altimira to protect United’s lead as Sporting battled to find an equaliser.

It eventually came from a howler from Lammens, who failed to claim a cross dropping out of the sky, spilling the ball in front of Suarez, who produced a hooked acrobatic effort to score.

Moments later United had the ball in the net at the other end after another goalkeeping error by Pereira, who mishandled Fernandes’s corner, pushing the ball into his own net.

Fernandes sent United ahead with a lucky bounce taking his effort over the Sporting goalkeeper, before Suarez’s acrobatic effort levelled the game.

United midfielder Youri Tielemans was sent off in stoppage time for a second yellow card to end a compelling and often erratic match.

A crushing 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool in the Premier League at the weekend, leaving United 19th, was a disastrous first game at the helm for Pochettino after replacing Michael Carrick.

Pochettino brought Harry Maguire into the three-man defence as he shuffled his pack, as well as starting Joshua Zirkzee in place of the suspended Matheus Cunha.

Neither side took many risks in the opening stages, with few chances of note until the game burst into life midway through the first half as United lost control.

Lisandro Martinez brought down Geny Catamo in the area and Sporting were awarded a penalty.

The hosts blew their chance from the spot, with Suarez’s scuffed effort easily saved by Lammens, but the Red Devils gave away another spot kick just a couple of minutes later.

Goalkeeper Lammens came flying off his line and clattered Maxi Araujo, and this time Colombian striker Suarez made no mistake from the spot.

United thought they had equalised when Amad Diallo hit the crossbar and then nodded home the rebound, but the goal was disallowed to their dismay.

Youri Tielemans was ruled to have fouled Goncalo Inacio, although he seemed to win the ball, upsetting United further after Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool on Sunday that was later rescinded.

Fernandes pulled United level early in the second half from the spot after Eduardo Quaresma brought down Martinez.

The former Sporting playmaker calmly stroked his penalty beyond the dive of Kaique Pereira into the bottom left corner.

Fernandes said on the eve of the game he had stopped contract talks because he wanted to focus on helping United improve their form after a dire start to the season.

The midfielder soon had his second goal, with the help of a bizarre bounce off a divot on the pitch.

Fernandes’s low effort from distance seemed bound for Pereira’s hands, but suddenly bounced up off a patch of uneven turf and fortuitously over the goalkeeper’s head.

The Portugal international bent a free-kick narrowly off target as he looked to complete his hat-trick.

Lammens saved well from Sergi Altimira to protect United’s lead as Sporting battled to find an equaliser.

It eventually came from a howler from Lammens, who failed to claim a cross dropping out of the sky, spilling the ball in front of Suarez, who produced a hooked acrobatic effort to score.

Moments later United had the ball in the net at the other end after another goalkeeping error by Pereira, who mishandled Fernandes’s corner, pushing the ball into his own net.

น่าน.title: Fernandes shines on Sporting return as Man United held
น่าน.summary:
LISBON, Nov 25 : Bruno Fernandes set aside questions about his Manchester United future by producing his best display of the season against his former club Sporting on Wednesday, scoring twice in a chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw.

Fernandes's goals looked set to earn Mauricio Pochettino a first win a week after taking charge, but United were undone by two shambolic mistakes from goalkeeper Senne Lammens in a contest that also featured three penalties, two disallowed United goals and a late red card for Youri Tielemans.

While frustrated not to claim all three points, both Fernandes and Pochettino found reasons for encouragement in a performance that suggested the troubled side may finally be moving in the right direction.

"So proud of my players, it was a really tough game, and I like the team, the personality, the character," Pochettino said.

"We were again punished a lot in different actions that were key. I think we showed the way that we want to play, it's only one week working together. I feel so proud. I told them after the game."

With speculation over his United future, Fernandes had said on Tuesday that contract talks could wait until results improve.

The Portugal midfielder, whose contract expires at the end of the season but includes a one-year option, had said he was focused on helping lift United out of their malaise.

"For us to start winning games, and then we can start speaking about (my) contract. That's not important now; it's irrelevant," Fernandes said. "I'm more worried about getting results, trying to bring the club back in a position to be proud of."

The 32-year-old more than did his part in a match that swung wildly.

Lammens first rescued United by saving a poor Luis Suarez penalty attempt, but barely a minute later conceded a second spot kick by fouling Maxi Araujo, allowing Suarez to put Sporting ahead.

Amad Diallo had a goal disallowed for a foul in the buildup, and then Fernandes scored twice in three minutes after the break to put United in front, his first from the penalty spot and his second a long-range shot that wrongfooted goalkeeper Kaique after hitting a divot in the pitch.

Lammens allowed Suarez to level when he inexplicably spilled a high ball in the 80th minute and the Colombian forward pounced to make it 2-2. United's frustration was compounded when a late Sporting own goal was ruled out following a VAR review.

"Mistakes are part of football, and from that you get goals," said Fernandes, who was playing his first game against his former team since United paid 47 million pounds ($62 million) to sign him in January 2020.

"It's not an individual sport ... the most important thing is that we understand that we need to be together in the good and in the bad moments, and it's not going to change the belief we have in Senne."

While frustrated not to claim all three points, Fernandes said the display was encouraging ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash with Brentford, with United languishing in the relegation zone.

"Obviously, it's massive for us every game," said the Portugal midfielder. "Now the moment is to get back to the Premier League, and understanding that our position there is fragile, we need to really stick together, understanding that we need to fight for our lives because at the moment that's our situation."

น่าน.title: Commentary: Will it be a three or even two-horse race in Singapore's telco sector?
น่าน.summary:
2026 has seen a pivotal shift in Singapore’s telco landscape, with the industry now shaping up to be a two-and-a-half horse race, says former editor and financial journalist Ven Sreenivasan.

SINGAPORE: It has been quite an eventful year for the local telecommunications sector.

After months of speculation, StarHub and M1 – Singapore’s second and third-biggest telcos – confirmed on Tuesday (Nov 24) that they will combine in an all-share deal worth S$1.1 billion.

The combined group – which will take shape upon completion of the merger in 2027 following regulatory approval – will oversee 4.1 million mobile customers and over 750,000 broadband users.

Separately on Tuesday, StarHub also exercised an option to buy Circles.Life’s Singapore mobile business. This follows the telco’s recent acquisition of MyRepublic’s mobile business.

So, the sector is officially down to three big players, much like a decade ago: The proposed StarHub-M1 entity; market leader Singtel, which has 4.5 million mobile customers and 700,000 broadband subscribers; and Simba with 1.4 million mobile subscribers, although questions have emerged over its future over regulatory breaches.

Even with the spectacular collapse of the Simba-M1 deal in May, the general consensus among experts has been that consolidation remains on the card in Singapore’s small and extremely saturated market.

Since 2020, the industry has seen aggressive price competition, with providers slashing mobile plan prices following the entry of Simba, formerly TPG. Then came along a slew of mobile virtual network players like MyRepublic and Circles.Life, all jostling for a slice of a market of just 6 million users.

In economics, one is taught that competition is good. But can there be too much of it? Falling mobile service revenues suggest so.

StarHub’s third-quarter mobile service revenue fell 6 per cent from a year ago amid competition from rivals offering “heavily discounted plans”. Combined with first half of the year, revenue is down 9 per cent year-on-year.

Over at Singtel, its Singapore mobile service revenue grew an on-quarter 3.8 per cent in the second quarter, its second consecutive quarter of sequential growth. This, however, came after seven quarters of decline.

These highlight the pains of an aggressive price war and the need for a reset.

Top telco executives here pointed to industry consolidation elsewhere in the region.

At a results briefing in May, Singtel’s chief executive Yuen Kuan Moon was reported as saying it “would not be sustainable for Singapore to have four telco operators”, a figure that is more than that in larger markets like Thailand, Indonesia and India that have already undergone consolidation.

This week, StarHub CEO Nikhil Eapen described the chapter of liberalisation in Singapore’s telco market as “now closing”.

The uncertainty that remains following a year of twists and turns is the fate of Simba.

The telco, which emerged as a credible challenger to the incumbents since its entry, came under regulatory scrutiny in May. Then, the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) said it had uncovered a potential regulatory breach involving the unauthorised use of spectrum bands, while assessing Simba’s proposed acquisition of M1.

น่าน.title: Nvidia halts server shipments to Southeast Asia
น่าน.summary:
Manufacturers ordered to stop shipping hardware with Nvidia chips to Thailand and 3 other countries

Nvidia has told ​its manufacturing partners ‌to stop shipping servers containing its chips to Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported ​on Thursday.

​Manufacturing partners including Dell and Supermicro, which package Nvidia chips into servers, ⁠have told buyers in the four countries that the chip maker would not allow their orders to ​be shipped, the report said, citing three people familiar with the matter.

It was unclear whether the halt would be temporary as Nvidia and its partners ‌work through compliance requirements under new US export controls, the newspaper said.

Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Nvidia, Dell and Supermicro did not immediately respond to ⁠requests for comment outside regular business hours.

The US Commerce Department last week imposed a rule affecting shipments of advanced AI chips to countries where US officials believe Chinese companies have used data centres to access computing power for training AI models.

The department published the rule days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following ⁠reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who ​previously worked at the Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed. Nvidia’s board subsequently reinstated Huang as CEO on Nov 23.

Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner that rents computing power at its data centres, has come ‌under scrutiny for ⁠possible illegal diversion of advanced AI ​chips to China.

The new rules also eliminated a compliance pathway that had allowed some Chinese chip designers to access advanced manufacturing services without obtaining individual export licences, further tightening restrictions on China’s ​access to advanced AI chips.

The measures are part of Washington’s efforts to crack down on ​overseas ‌data centres and chip smuggling routes amid growing scrutiny of whether enough is being done to prevent sensitive US technology ​from ⁠reaching China.

Renting AI computing power from data centres that run on US hardware not available for export to China is one way Chinese developers are believed to be getting around US restrictions.

Under the new rule, data centres anywhere in the world will need a US licence to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.

The rule also requires licences to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, which the Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion”.

น่าน.title: Woman in China Jailed for Tossing Coins at Planes Engine
น่าน.summary:
WUHAN, China — Chinese police detained a 61-year-old woman for five days after she threw four coins toward a passenger jet for good luck during boarding at Wuhan Tianhe International Airport, forcing an emergency safety sweep that delayed departure by 58 minutes.

The Nov. 16 incident disrupted a family flight bound for Sanya on Hainan Island and prompted a fresh warning from aviation authorities. Officials are cracking down on the persistent folk ritual because loose metal sucked into high-speed jet engines can shatter turbine blades and trigger catastrophic midair failure.

• Police jailed a 61-year-old first-time flyer for five days under public order laws after she tossed four coins toward her aircraft in Wuhan.

• Nearly 10 maintenance workers inspected the tarmac and engines, delaying the Hainan-bound flight by 58 minutes before clearing it for takeoff.

The disruption began as the passenger, identified only by her surname Zhou, boarded the aircraft with three relatives while carrying a young child. Reaching the cabin threshold, she pulled four coins from her pocket and tossed them toward the nose of the jet. The coins slipped through the narrow gap between the jet bridge and the fuselage, landing on the concrete apron below.

A sharp-eyed flight attendant spotted the toss and immediately notified the cockpit and ground crew. Airline staff halted boarding at once. According to local media reports, nearly 10 maintenance technicians fanned out across the tarmac to recover every coin and inspect the aircraft’s engines for hidden debris before the plane could push back.

Hubei Airport Police escorted Zhou off the flight for questioning. She told investigators she was flying for the first time and had acted on an old folk custom that tossing coins while crossing a bridge ensures safe passage. Officers charged her under Article 26 of China’s Public Security Administration Punishments Law for disrupting order on public transportation, ordering five days of administrative detention. Zhou later expressed regret and urged police to share her case online so other travelers would not repeat her mistake.

Zhou’s arrest reflects a recurring clash between traditional Chinese blessing rituals and modern commercial aviation. For generations, travelers in China have tossed coins into temple wells, river crossings and wishing pools for protection. As domestic air travel expanded rapidly over the past decade, millions of older, first-time flyers entered airports for the first time, occasionally treating boarding bridges and gleaming turbine cowlings like good-luck shrines.

Aviation records show the pattern spans multiple airlines and hubs. In 2017, an 80-year-old passenger delayed a China Southern Airlines flight in Shanghai for more than five hours after throwing nine coins at an engine. Two years later, authorities detained two women after a Lucky Air flight in eastern China was grounded for two hours over a similar coin toss. Even steep fines have not stopped the habit; courts in several provinces have ordered offending passengers to pay carriers tens of thousands of yuan in delay damages.

To aviation engineers, a single coin poses an acute mechanical threat known as foreign object debris. Running jet engines generate immense intake suction, pulling loose tarmac items into compressor blades spinning at thousands of revolutions per minute.

น่าน.title: Trump's accounts traded Nvidia shares 44 times this year, records show
น่าน.summary:
Donald Trump's investment portfolios have bought or sold shares in chipmaker Nvidia at least 44 times this year, a review of the US president's financial disclosures shows.

Trump's most recent public declarations of his investment trading show that between January and September the portfolios purchased between $5.2m and $17m (Â£4m and Â£13m) in Nvidia stock - and sold between $4.4m and $12m. His portfolios held between $12.5m and $58m of Nvidia shares at the end of 2025.

Financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics report a low and high range of transaction values, so a more precise analysis of how much Nvidia stock was traded is not possible.

The period of recent turmoil at Nvidia and volatility in its share price is not covered by the disclosures. In the last two weeks, co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang resigned and then Trump played a significant part in his reinstatement.

The White House has said that Trump's stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third parties and neither he nor his family "has any ability to direct, influence or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold".

Huang resigned on 12 November after reports of extramarital affairs, including with one woman who has alleged ties to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia's share price dived following news of his resignation.

But on Monday Nvidia's board announced the 63-year-old was being reinstated as CEO.

Trump told US media he had "made the deal" to "convince" the tech giant's board to bring Huang back. The board said it had "received input from senior levels of the United States government" that he posed "no national security risk".

Nvidia's share price surged 31% on Monday following Huang's return. About $1tn (Â£763bn) was added to Nvidia's market value, but the company's shares are still trading below their value before reports of Huang's alleged affairs began to circulate.

However, concerns remain among both Republican and Democratic politicians about Huang's actions and Nvidia's compliance with US controls over the export of advanced computer chips to China, as well as Trump's involvement in getting him reappointed as CEO.

Nvidia's chip technology and investments have been critical to the growth of the artificial intelligence (AI) industry, leading to it becoming one of the world's most valuable companies.

The firm now represents more than 6% of the S&P 500 share index, according to State Street financial services. This makes it the second most valuable company on the index after Apple, whose shares Trump's accounts also frequently trade.

Nvidia also ranks highly in many global indices, meaning that investment accounts held around the world, including pensions, are likely to include its shares.

Our analysis of Trump's Nvidia trades does not include other investment products held by him which may include its shares.

Trump made at least $2.2bn (Â£1.7bn) from a variety of investments and commercial activities, according to the financial disclosure report for the first year of Trump's second term.

Barbara Perry, a presidential historian at the University of Virginia's Miller Center, told the BBC there is "no precedent for this," adding: "It's beyond anything we've ever seen in the presidency."

Huang resigned on 12 November after reports of extramarital affairs, including with one woman who has alleged ties to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia's share price dived following news of his resignation.

But on Monday Nvidia's board announced the 63-year-old was being reinstated as CEO.

Trump told US media he had "made the deal" to "convince" the tech giant's board to bring Huang back. The board said it had "received input from senior levels of the United States government" that he posed "no national security risk".

Nvidia's share price surged 31% on Monday following Huang's return. About $1tn (Â£763bn) was added to Nvidia's market value, but the company's shares are still trading below their value before reports of Huang's alleged affairs began to circulate.

However, concerns remain among both Republican and Democratic politicians about Huang's actions and Nvidia's compliance with US controls over the export of advanced computer chips to China, as well as Trump's involvement in getting him reappointed as CEO.

Nvidia's chip technology and investments have been critical to the growth of the artificial intelligence (AI) industry, leading to it becoming one of the world's most valuable companies.

The firm now represents more than 6% of the S&P 500 share index, according to State Street financial services. This makes it the second most valuable company on the index after Apple, whose shares Trump's accounts also frequently trade.

Nvidia also ranks highly in many global indices, meaning that investment accounts held around the world, including pensions, are likely to include its shares.

Our analysis of Trump's Nvidia trades does not include other investment products held by him which may include its shares.

Trump made at least $2.2bn (Â£1.7bn) from a variety of investments and commercial activities, according to the financial disclosure report for the first year of Trump's second term.

Barbara Perry, a presidential historian at the University of Virginia's Miller Center, told the BBC there is "no precedent for this," adding: "It's beyond anything we've ever seen in the presidency."

ตามมาด้วย The Darkest Romance ที่ยกระดับความดุดันเข้มข้นไปกับเพลงใหม่อย่าง ดีบุก ซัดพลังเสียงกระแทกใจคนดูแบบไม่ให้พักหายใจไปกับเพลง ความรู้สึกผิด และ ความรุนแรง พร้อมสร้างโมเมนต์สุดพิเศษเมื่อ “แม็ก” ลงมาเล่นท่ามกลางวงล้อมของแฟนเพลง ให้ทุกคนได้มีส่วนร่วมและปลดปล่อยอารมณ์ไปพร้อมกันอย่างใกล้ชิดในเพลง “ความเยาว์”

Under the main “Section 301” probe into excess industrial capacity, China would face the highest capped rate of 20%, which would be added to duties of roughly 25% imposed during Trump’s first term.
That rate would comply with a US-China trade truce that expires on January 10. But if the truce unravels, China’s rate would rise to 40%, the USTR said.

Washington has long accused China of subsidizing industry and flooding global markets with low-cost exports ranging from steel to electric vehicles and solar products.
Beijing earlier reiterated its opposition to “trade wars” and rejected allegations of overcapacity, but stopped short of threatening retaliation.

“The so-called ‘overcapacity’ is a false issue, and China opposes using it as an excuse for political manipulation,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said, urging the world’s top two economies to maintain stable relations.

They know what we’re proposing. I think a lot of this is baked in.”

Mexico and Norway were excluded from the proposals because investigations into their trade practices remain under way, Greer said.

Even so, the prospect of new trade barriers weighed on stock markets on Wednesday amid a renewed selloff in tech stocks. Major US indexes opened down more than 1%, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite .IXIC down more than 3%.

“It is another reminder that while the legal justification for tariffs keeps changing, US protectionism is becoming increasingly difficult to unwind,” ING analysts wrote.

NEW DUTIES WON’T EXCEED NEGOTIATED LIMITS

Trump’s tariffs have contributed to higher prices for US consumers, and a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll conducted after Republicans’ midterm losses found 62% of respondents supported efforts to repeal them.

But Trump has long vowed to restore duties struck down by the US Supreme Court in February. The latest measures follow an eight-month investigation into unfair trade practices under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

Greer said the proposed tariffs would not apply to about $30 billion of Chinese imports under consideration for tariff reductions through a bilateral mechanism known as the Board of Trade.

However, the new duties would be added to tariffs imposed on Chinese goods during Trump’s first term, which total roughly 25%.

They would not be imposed on top of the 10% and 12.5% tariffs introduced in July on a broader group of 60 trading partners over allegations of lax enforcement of anti-forced-labor laws.

ตาก.title: The painful souvenir many tourists take home from Thailand
ตาก.summary:
If you’ve spent any time around Thailand’s tourist hotspots, you’ve probably spotted a few foreign visitors walking around with bandages wrapped around their legs. It’s common enough to make you wonder what’s going on.

One X user wondered the same thing and decided to ask the question.

@Berlusconnii posed the question in Portuguese, wondering why so many tourists in Thailand seem to have wounds on their legs. He accompanied the post with a video showing foreign visitors sporting bandages on their legs.

“Alguém me explica por que quase todo turista na Tailândia tem um machucado na perna? 🤔🇹🇭🩹“

Most commenters pointed to a familiar holiday mishap: motorbike exhaust burns. Tourists who rent motorbikes often accidentally brush their legs against the hot exhaust pipes, leaving painful burns that can take time to heal.

Some commenters jokingly suggested that the marks were tattoos, but the more likely explanation is the hot exhaust pipes of rental motorbikes.

In Thailand, these injuries are something of a familiar sight among tourists, and have even become a running joke associated with renting a motorbike.

For some less fortunate riders, the bandages can cover considerably more than a burnt leg. Sometimes, they’re the result of a full-blown motorbike crash.

But even a nasty spill doesn’t always seem to convince some travellers to wear a helmet or dress appropriately for the ride.

ตาก.title: Thailand Urges Year-End Vigilance as Three Illnesses Spread
ตาก.summary:
BANGKOK — Thailand’s Department of Disease Control has urged residents and holiday travelers to take basic health precautions through the end of the year as seasonal influenza circulates widely, pertussis clusters persist in the south and mpox infections climb steadily.

Surveillance records compiled by the agency’s Division of Epidemiology show 645,874 reported influenza cases through mid-November, alongside 470 cumulative mpox infections and three deaths logged in the first 10 months of 2026. Health officials said cooler weather and heavy domestic travel ahead of New Year celebrations could accelerate transmission, though individual risk varies sharply by age, vaccination status and local exposure.

Seasonal shifts explain part of the year-end pattern. Upper Thailand entered its cool season in early November, prompting people to spend more time in enclosed, air-conditioned rooms, buses and classrooms where respiratory droplets linger. Earlier this year, Department of Disease Control Director-General Dr. Montien Kanasawat warned that school terms and holiday transit corridors consistently amplify flu spread, especially among children ages 5 to 9.

Whooping cough, known medically as pertussis, follows a different geographic fault line. While largely controlled in central provinces, public health teams in late November monitored more than 130 diphtheria and pertussis cases and six deaths across Thailand’s three southernmost border provinces. Epidemiological studies show lower routine immunization uptake in parts of the deep south, combined with waning immunity among adults whose childhood shots have faded over time.

Mpox transmission remains concentrated in close-contact networks rather than casual public spaces. Deputy Director-General Dr. Direk Khampaen noted that while most patients recover without specialized hospital care, Thailand’s international travel links mean imported and local cases continue to appear steadily.

Distinguishing these illnesses early helps patients isolate before passing germs to vulnerable relatives. Influenza usually strikes abruptly with high fever, body aches, chills, sore throat and fatigue. Most healthy adults recover within a week.

Pertussis begins like a mild cold with a runny nose and low fever. After one to two weeks, however, patients develop violent coughing fits that can end in vomiting, exhaustion or a high-pitched gasping sound. In infants under 1 year old, the infection can trigger dangerous pauses in breathing rather than an obvious cough.

Mpox often starts with fever, headache, backache and swollen lymph nodes before skin lesions emerge on the face, hands, body, genitals or anus. Officials stressed that some patients develop only a few spots without fever, and laboratory PCR swabs of skin lesions are required because visual inspection alone cannot confirm the virus.

Health officials emphasize steady, everyday habits over panic. Annual flu vaccinations remain free at state clinics for high-risk groups, including pregnant women, young children, seniors and people with chronic heart or lung conditions. Parents should check their children’s pink health booklets to ensure routine diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis doses are current, while pregnant women are advised to receive a pertussis booster to shield newborns.

ตาก.title: Bangkok Chao Phraya Dinner Cruises: Prices and Tips
ตาก.summary:
Bangkok’s riverside temples and landmarks take on a different look after dark, making a Chao Phraya dinner cruise an easy way to see the city from the water. Options range from casual buffet boats with live entertainment to premium experiences aboard restored rice barges, such as Anantara Riverside’s restored-rice-barge dinner cruise.

Prices vary widely, and the lowest headline fare may not include drinks or other extras. This guide compares cruise styles, November 2026 price ranges, and the booking details that can affect your evening, including the pier, schedule, and ticket inclusions.

Most Bangkok dinner cruises spend about two hours on the Chao Phraya River, combining an evening meal with views of the city’s riverfront. Depending on the boat and direction of travel, passengers may see Wat Arun, the Grand Palace area, and Rama VIII Bridge. The route, visibility, meal, and entertainment vary by operator, and weather can affect the views from open decks.

A buffet ticket usually includes a mix of Thai and international dishes, with menus varying by cruise. Some boats add seafood, such as prawns or other seafood selections, while live music and Thai dance performances may be part of the evening. Large vessels often have several decks, including open-air areas where guests can watch the riverfront pass by.

That lively setup suits travelers who enjoy a broad menu and shared entertainment. For a look at the riverside landmarks along Bangkok’s boat routes, remember that a dinner cruise offers passing views rather than time ashore at each site. Boats may pass Wat Arun and the Grand Palace area before continuing toward Rama VIII Bridge; one cruise operator’s route highlights also include these landmarks.

Check the ticket details before booking, especially for drinks. Some packages include selected beverages, but others charge separately for beer, wine, or soft drinks. A seafood buffet or free-flow offer may also apply only to a specific ticket tier, so compare the inclusions for your sailing rather than relying on a general description.

Manohra offers a different pace aboard a restored rice barge, with a Thai set menu and a smaller-scale feel than a large buffet boat. It lists three two-hour dinner rounds, departing at 6:00, 7:00, and 8:30 p.m. That range can help guests choose an earlier meal or a later evening on the river.

The higher price reflects the set-menu format and boat experience, but it doesn’t automatically include alcoholic drinks. Manohra’s listed packages distinguish between free-flow soft drinks and options that include wine and beer. Check the current menu and package terms before booking, since inclusions can differ even within the same operator.

Neither style suits every traveler. A buffet cruise brings more food choices and a livelier deck, while a set-menu barge offers a more measured dinner with fewer guests around. Compare the meal format, drink allowance, sailing time, and expected atmosphere to find the ticket that fits your evening.

In November 2026, Chao Phraya dinner cruises range from about THB 900 for a budget buffet ticket to more than THB 5,000 per person for a premium set menu with drinks. Treat these figures as a price snapshot, not guaranteed fares: the amount can change by sailing date, seller, guest category, and package inclusions.

Manohra offers a different pace aboard a restored rice barge, with a Thai set menu and a smaller-scale feel than a large buffet boat. It lists three two-hour dinner rounds, departing at 6:00, 7:00, and 8:30 p.m. That range can help guests choose an earlier meal or a later evening on the river.

The higher price reflects the set-menu format and boat experience, but it doesn’t automatically include alcoholic drinks. Manohra’s listed packages distinguish between free-flow soft drinks and options that include wine and beer. Check the current menu and package terms before booking, since inclusions can differ even within the same operator.

Neither style suits every traveler. A buffet cruise brings more food choices and a livelier deck, while a set-menu barge offers a more measured dinner with fewer guests around. Compare the meal format, drink allowance, sailing time, and expected atmosphere to find the ticket that fits your evening.

In November 2026, Chao Phraya dinner cruises range from about THB 900 for a budget buffet ticket to more than THB 5,000 per person for a premium set menu with drinks. Treat these figures as a price snapshot, not guaranteed fares: the amount can change by sailing date, seller, guest category, and package inclusions.

ตาก.title: Taking Cash Across Thailand’s Borders: What to Declare
ตาก.summary:
Carrying cash into or out of Thailand can raise questions at Customs, especially if you have several currencies or are crossing a land border. The amount that triggers a declaration depends on the currency and the rules that apply to your route. Chiang Rai Times reports that travelers carrying more than USD 20,000, or its equivalent in foreign currency, must report it when entering or leaving Thailand. Because Customs requirements can change, check the current guidance before you travel. A declaration is a report to Customs; by itself, it does not mean you’re barred from carrying the money.

The available Chiang Rai Times guidance says travelers must report foreign currency worth more than USD 20,000, or its equivalent, when entering or leaving Thailand. It describes this as a combined value across foreign currencies, rather than a separate allowance for each currency. For example, if you carry U.S. dollars and euros, the relevant calculation may involve their combined value.

The guidance covers physical banknotes and coins carried by a traveler or packed in baggage traveling on the same conveyance. It does not treat bank balances or payment cards as cash carried across the border. For details, see Thailand’s cash declaration rules for travelers.

Because Customs requirements can change, check the current Thai Customs guidance before your trip, especially if your cash total is close to the reporting threshold. Confirm what applies to your specific travel date and crossing. A report to Customs is not automatically a ban on carrying the money, but you should check for any separate restrictions that may apply to your circumstances.

The published guidance gives a USD 20,000 equivalent figure. Before relying on it, confirm the current requirement with Thai Customs, including whether it applies to your route and the currencies you’re carrying. Don’t assume an old article or a threshold remembered from a previous trip reflects the rules in force when you travel.

The available guidance refers to physical banknotes and coins. Count the currency you’ll carry yourself and any cash packed in baggage traveling with you. If you plan to carry a financial instrument other than banknotes or coins, ask Thai Customs how it is treated rather than assuming it follows the same rule.

Thai baht and foreign currency are separate considerations. The foreign-currency reporting guidance does not, by itself, tell you how much Thai baht you may carry across a border. Check Thai Customs’ current rules for baht and the requirements of the country you’re entering.

This matters whether you’re flying or crossing a land border. The next country may have its own rules for bringing in Thai baht, and those rules don’t disappear because you’ve checked Thailand’s requirements. Before you travel, consult the customs authority for your destination as well as Thai Customs.

A reported incident at the Mae Sai 1st Friendship Bridge involved Customs seizing 3,572,240 baht from a traveler. That case illustrates why travelers should take border rules seriously, but an incident report does not establish a general allowance or reporting threshold. Check the rules for your own circumstances instead of using a reported seizure as a guide.

ตาก.title: Protesters call on Israel to free Palestinian student held without charge
ตาก.summary:
Israeli students, activists and academics are calling for the release of a Palestinian undergraduate who was taken from his university dormitory by Israeli police earlier this month and has since been held without charge.

Mahdi Tunsi, a 26-year-old sociology and criminology student at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, appeared in an Israeli court in the city on Tuesday - a hearing that was held behind closed doors.

Israeli police say he was arrested "concerning ties to an act of terrorism".

Authorities have requested what is known as "administrative detention", which allows the Israeli state to detain people indefinitely without charge on the basis of secret evidence that they cannot see.

"We definitely think this is a political arrest," said Dr Yael Berda, one of Tunsi's university professors.

Tunsi, a Palestinian resident of occupied East Jerusalem who works with well-known Jewish-Palestinian campaign groups, was arrested a month after Israel held an election that saw Arab-led parties win a record 19 seats in parliament, the Knesset, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing coalition lose its majority.

Since then, Berda said she had seen an intensifying campaign against Palestinian rights.

Outside the Jerusalem District Court on Tuesday, demonstrators waved placards with a black-and-white image of Tunsi, while crying out "shame" in unison.

"There's no due process - [administrative detention is] a sugar-coated term for being kidnapped and held as a hostage," said Dr Ofer Cassif, a Member of the Knesset representing the Arab-led Joint List alliance.

"We must all stand firm against such crimes. It's unacceptable."

Since the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, which triggered the Gaza war, the number of people in administrative detention has more than doubled.

In October, there were more than 3,100 in administrative detention, according to Israel Prison Service figures published by Israeli rights group HaMoked. Most of them are Palestinians from the occupied West Bank.

Israel says that its use of the policy is compliant with international law and a necessary preventative measure to combat terrorism.

In a statement, Israeli police said they would "not elaborate further regarding the investigation" into Tunsi.

He appeared via video link from prison - his hair and beard shaved off. His friends also said that he was without medication as well as his glasses, despite a judge requesting them to be brought to him in detention.

The Israel Prison Service said it acted in accordance with the court's rulings.

"When the process was complete and all the necessary approvals had been received, the detainee's lawyer was told he could pass the eyeglasses to the detainee immediately, subject to security procedures," it added.

Berda asked to enter the courtroom on Tuesday but was denied entry. According to Berda, not even Tunsi has been told of the evidence against him.

The judge has said more time is needed to consider the state's request for administrative detention. A decision is expected in the coming days.

"If they have evidence, have them bring it or release him," said Berda.

"That's why we're demanding his immediate release or moving it to a criminal track where he could defend himself."

Berda said that while Tunsi could not vote in Israel's general election because he is not an Israeli citizen, he was "engaged" and very supportive of Arab parties' involvement.

ตาก.title: Iraq’s top court rules government can take over Kurdish borders, oil fields
ตาก.summary:
Iraq’s top court has ruled that the federal government can deploy troops to the country’s international borders, including in the semi-autonomous Kurdish region.

Wednesday’s ruling comes a day after Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered federal forces to take over Kurdish-run border crossings and demanded authority over oil fields controlled by Kurdish security forces, in an effort to curb oil smuggling.

Kurdish authorities denounced the move, with the regional government calling it “an assault” on the region’s “constitutional rights”.

The Federal ⁠⁠⁠⁠Supreme Court also ruled that federal authorities could oversee agencies operating at all border crossings, including those in northern Iraq’s Kurdish region, though they must coordinate with regional and provincial governments on customs administration, state television reported.

The court said the federal oil ministry can also oversee and audit oil and gas fields, while Baghdad shares responsibility for managing the oil and gas they produce with regional governments and producing provinces, according to state TV.

The Iraqi government did not specify how or when the takeover would be implemented.

The move comes just a week after al-Zaidi also took on Kataib Hezbollah – a powerful Shia militia aligned with Iran – following oil smuggling allegations.

He ordered troops to prepare to enter the city of Jurf al-Sakhar, a Kataib stronghold south of Baghdad. The group initially responded with defiance but allowed soldiers into the city, following a compromise brokered by Shia politicians.

The court’s decision appears to be a victory for al-Zaidi, but analysts say it will be challenging to implement moves against the Kurds and the heavily armed Shia militias loyal to Iran.

Renad Mansour, deputy director of the Middle East and ‌‌‌‌North Africa programme and director of the Iraq Initiative at Chatham House, said Iraq’s judiciary was “very much supportive” of the government’s campaign to establish a centralised political order.

“The Iraqi government [is] trying to reclaim some sovereignty … because it’s such a fragmented state where there isn’t a centre,” he said.

A senior Shia politician close to Zaidi told the Reuters news agency that the prime minister was trying to dismantle the model of a “state within a state”. He added that al-Zaidi was trying to restrain armed factions operating above state authority, as well as draw clearer limits on the semi-autonomous Kurdish region’s exercise of authority over strategic economic and security matters.

The Kurdistan Regional Government on Wednesday rejected what it called “military ⁠⁠⁠⁠language and threats” in a statement from the Iraqi military announcing the new measures. It said ⁠⁠⁠⁠it was working with federal authorities to combat corruption and called for an end to oil smuggling across Iraq.

Iraq’s state news agency, citing what it said was a federal government intelligence report, said oil belonging to the state-owned North Oil Company was being diverted and smuggled from Kirkuk, as well as from Sulaimaniyah inside Iraq’s Kurdish region, to Iran and onward to Afghanistan.

Also on Wednesday, the Syrian and Iraqi defence ministers discussed “several issues of mutual interest” over the phone, according to Syria’s Ministry of Defence.

ตาก.title: Commentary: From solving to ‘digesting’: How mathematicians can adapt to the dramatic changes of AI
ตาก.summary:
If AI can generate papers that would take a human mathematician years to research and write, does that mean mathematics is dead? A professor gives his take.

KNOXVILLE, Tennessee: Mathematics is having an existential crisis.

On Nov 20, 2026, a mathematician at the AI company Anthropic claimed that while working with the model Claude, he had solved the generalised Riemann hypothesis, the most famous problem in mathematics. This problem has stood unsolved for 167 years, and solving it could easily warrant a Fields Medal – considered equivalent to a Nobel Prize, but for mathematics. In its current state, however, the solution is roughly 250,000 pages long, so it will take a while before human mathematicians can be satisfied that it is correct.

This proof emerged a month after OpenAI released 722 mathematics research papers that contained results generated by an internal AI model. While they have already retracted some of the papers due to mistakes, others, assuming they are correct, would also be impressive enough to earn a Fields Medal.

If AI can generate papers that would take a human mathematician years to research and write, does that mean mathematics is dead? Many headlines have been asking this question – and some school-age children may be rejoicing.

But it’s not that simple. I’ve been a mathematician for 45 years, and my work has taught me that mathematics is not just about solving problems or proving theorems. It is about understanding why the solutions and proofs work and then extending that mathematics to new contexts.

Fueling this existential crisis is the fact that over the past century, mathematicians have come to attach greater prestige to the solution and the proof than the understanding. Now that an AI can come up with a solution and a proof, the underlying understanding could vanish. Mathematicians are being forced to rethink what they value.

If you’re not a mathematician, this crisis might seem inconsequential. But math isn’t all abstract problems. It’s used to design and optimise technology that’s essential to modern society.

One example is MRI, or magnetic resonance imaging. MRI is a very useful tool in medical diagnosis. X-rays see only your bones, but MRI machines allow a physician to see the soft tissue inside a person in a noninvasive manner.

MRI scans used to require a patient to lie still inside a metal tube for up to half an hour or more while a loud machine made images by scanning back and forth. At the end, it combined the images. This process was difficult for many adults and virtually impossible for children without sedation.

Modern MRI machines require many fewer scans in a shorter period, and they get better resolution. Now, more patients find the procedure no big deal. The key to this vast improvement was the mathematics of compressed sensing, a relatively recent invention.

Compressed sensing allows the machine to construct an image from fewer scans. At first, doing so didn’t seem possible. But in the mid 2000s, a mathematician, statisticians and an electrical engineer figured out how to use the fact that many of the scans are very similar to develop the mathematics that made compressed sensing possible.

ตาก.title: Saudi PIF looking to sell minority stake in Newcastle: report
ตาก.summary:
LONDON: The Saudi sovereign wealth fund is seeking to sell up to 25 per cent of Newcastle in order to fund major infrastructure investments at the Premier League club, the Athletic reported on Wednesday (Nov 25). A 2021 takeover led by the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF) has not had the transformative effect on the Magpies' fortunes that many fans dreamed of. The club won the League Cup - their first domestic trophy for 70 years - in 2025, and twice secured qualification for the Champions League. But they have been hampered by financial sustainability rules while recent cutbacks, including the withdrawal of funding for LIV Golf, suggest a change in strategy by the PIF. The British Reuben family owns around 16 per cent of Newcastle, with the remaining shares held by the PIF. The Athletic reported that fresh investment would be used to help fund an upgraded training facility and stadium redevelopment. In August, the club announced plans for a new £190 million (US$248 million) training ground that should be operational by the 2029/30 season. No decision has yet been made on whether to redevelop the 52,000-capacity St James' Park or build a new stadium. Yasir Al-Rumayyan, the PIF's governor and Newcastle chairman, attended his first match of the season on Saturday as Matthias Jaissle's men held defending champions Arsenal 2-2. Newcastle sit 13th in the Premier League table after a run of just one win in their past seven games in all competitions.

ตาก.title: สดจากเยาวชน – ต่างฝันต่างเติบโต ค่ายมวย‘ศิษย์ ด.ว.’
ตาก.summary:
เสียงหมัดกระทบเป้าซ้อม เสียงฝีเท้าที่ขยับไปมาบนพื้น และเสียงพูดคุยของเด็กๆ เป็นบรรยากาศคุ้นเคยของค่ายมวย “ศิษย์ ด.ว.” โรงเรียนด่านแม่ละเมาวิทยาคม อำเภอแม่สอด จังหวัดตาก พื้นที่เล็กๆ ที่รวมเด็กๆ ซึ่งสนใจกีฬามวยไทยและมวยสากลมาเรียนรู้และฝึกฝนร่วมกัน
ลงนวมเพิ่มทักษะ

เด็กแต่ละคนมีจุดเริ่มต้นและความฝันแตกต่างกัน โจวอยากมีโอกาสขึ้นชกบนเวทีลุมพินี เนตั้งเป้าหมายอยากคว้าแชมป์ราชดำเนิน ส่วนชาติฝันอยากเป็นนักมวยอาชีพเพื่อหาเงินเลี้ยงดูตัวเองและส่งให้แม่ ขณะที่กะทิเด็กหญิงเพียงคนเดียวในค่ายยังไม่เคยขึ้นชกบนเวทีจริง แต่อยากลองสัมผัสประสบการณ์นั้นสักครั้ง
แม้ความฝันจะต่างกัน แต่สิ่งที่เด็กๆ มีร่วมกันคือการฝึกฝนและพัฒนาตัวเองสม่ำเสมอ

“ซ้อมทุกวันครับ เริ่มตั้งแต่ประมาณ 16.30-20.30 น.” เนเล่าถึงกิจวัตรประจำวัน ก่อนอธิบายเพิ่มเติมว่าแม้จะผ่านการแข่งขันมาแล้วก็ยังต้องกลับมาฝึกซ้อมต่อหลังจากได้พักร่างกาย
ส่วนโจวมองว่าการฝึกซ้อมอย่างต่อเนื่องเป็นสิ่งสำคัญในการเตรียมตัวสำหรับการแข่งขัน โดยเฉพาะการวิ่งที่ช่วยเพิ่มความแข็งแรงและอดทน
“การวิ่งทำให้ร่างกายดีและทำให้แรงเรามีครับ เวลาขึ้นชกก็จะไม่เหนื่อย ทำให้ร่างกายเราอึดขึ้นครับ” โจวเล่า
ฝึกมวยกับโค้ชวิทย์

ภายใต้การดูแลของครูวิทย์ หรือสิบเอกไววิทย์ นารีรักษ์ อดีตนักกีฬามวยสากลสมัครเล่นทีมชาติไทย ศิษย์เก่าของโรงเรียน เด็กๆ เรียนรู้ทักษะการชกมวยตั้งแต่พื้นฐาน ทั้งการเคลื่อนไหว การออกหมัด การป้องกันตัว ไปจนถึงการฝึกความแข็งแรงและอดทน
แต่การฝึกมวยไม่ได้มีเพียงเรื่องทักษะและความแข็งแกร่งเท่านั้น เพราะระหว่างทางเด็กๆ ยังเรียนรู้การปรับตัว การอยู่ร่วมกับผู้อื่น และการสร้างความสัมพันธ์กับเพื่อนที่สนใจในสิ่งเดียวกัน
กะทิ นักเรียนชั้นมัธยมปลายซึ่งเพิ่งเข้ามาฝึกมวยได้ประมาณหนึ่งปี เล่าว่า ตอนแรกเธอคิดว่าจะได้เริ่มจากการชกกระสอบทรายทันที แต่ความจริงกลับต้องเริ่มเรียนรู้ใหม่ตั้งแต่การยืนทรงตัว การเคลื่อนที่ และการใช้หมัด
กะทิ สาวหนึ่งเดียว ใจนักสู้

“ตอนแรกคิดว่าเข้ามาจะได้ชกกระสอบเลย แต่ว่าไม่ใช่ เข้ามาก็คือเริ่มใหม่ตั้งแต่แรกเลย”
นอกจากต้องเรียนรู้ทักษะใหม่ๆ แล้ว กะทิยังต้องปรับตัวกับบรรยากาศการฝึกซ้อมที่ไม่คุ้นเคย
“ตอนแรกก็รู้สึกกลัวค่ะ แบบว่าเขาดูโหดกันมากเลย หลังๆ ไปก็ชินแล้วค่ะ เพราะว่าเห็นบ่อย”
แต่เมื่อได้ใช้เวลาร่วมกับเพื่อนๆ ในค่าย ความรู้สึกเหล่านั้นก็ค่อยๆ เปลี่ยนไป กะทิเล่าถึงความสัมพันธ์กับเพื่อนร่วมค่ายอย่างเรียบง่ายว่า “เพื่อนๆ ในค่ายก็สนิทกัน ดูแลกัน รู้จักกัน”
วิ่งฝึกความแกร่ง

คำพูดสั้นๆ นี้สะท้อนให้เห็นว่านอกจากการฝึกฝนเพื่อพัฒนาความสามารถแล้ว ค่ายมวยยังเป็นพื้นที่ให้เด็กๆ ทำความรู้จักและเรียนรู้การอยู่ร่วมกัน แม้แต่ละคนจะมีพื้นเพ ประสบการณ์ และเป้าหมายในชีวิตแตกต่างกัน
สำหรับโรงเรียนด่านแม่ละเมาวิทยาคมซึ่งมีทั้งนักเรียนในพื้นที่และนักเรียนประจำจากพื้นที่ห่างไกลหลากหลายชาติพันธุ์ การเปิดโอกาสให้เด็กๆ เลือกเรียนรู้ตามความสนใจจึงไม่ได้เป็นเพียงการส่งเสริมทักษะด้านกีฬา แต่ยังสร้างพื้นที่กิจกรรมที่ช่วยให้เด็กค้นพบความสามารถของตัวเอง
พื้นที่รวมเด็ก รวมใจ

ครูวิทย์มองว่ามวยเป็นทักษะที่ต่อยอดได้หลายทาง ไม่จำเป็นว่าทุกคนที่เรียนมวยจะต้องเป็นนักกีฬาอาชีพ เพราะความรู้ที่ได้รับยังนำไปใช้ออกกำลังกาย ป้องกันตัว หรือแม้แต่ถ่ายทอดให้ผู้อื่นในอนาคต
“ถ้าเราเรียนรู้จริงๆ มวยสามารถดัดแปลงได้หลายอย่าง ไม่ว่าจะเป็นการแข่งขัน ผู้ฝึกสอน หรือเป็นครูที่จะถ่ายทอดวิชาไปได้”
เช่นเดียวกับกะทิที่แม้จะยังไม่เคยขึ้นเวทีแข่งขัน แต่มีเป้าหมายเล็กๆ ของตัวเอง “อยากเตะเก่ง แล้วก็อยากออกอาวุธให้เก่งกว่านี้”
ฝึกซ้อมสู่ความแกร่ง

ความตั้งใจของกะทิอาจแตกต่างจากโจว เน ชาติ แต่มีความหมายไม่แพ้กัน เพราะการเติบโตของเด็กแต่ละคนไม่จำเป็นต้องวัดจากเป้าหมายเดียวกัน บางคนอยากเป็นแชมป์ บางคนอยากเป็นนักมวยอาชีพ ขณะที่บางคนเพียงอยากเก่งขึ้นกว่าตัวเองในวันก่อน
ท้ายที่สุดแล้ว เด็กๆ ค่ายมวยศิษย์ ด.ว. อาจเติบโตไปบนเส้นทางที่แตกต่างกัน แต่ช่วงเวลาฝึกซ้อม เรียนรู้ และใช้ชีวิตร่วมกัน เป็นประสบการณ์ช่วยให้พวกเขาค่อยๆ เติบโตทั้งในฐานะนักกีฬาและในฐานะคนคนหนึ่ง

ตาก.title: Thailand will not lend its sovereignty to anyone ‘even for a minute’, Anutin says
ตาก.summary:
Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on 26 November that Thailand’s armed forces were ready to defend the country and pledged government support for the weapons and equipment they need. He cited the experience of families in seven provinces along the Cambodian border who feared shelling in their sleep during the 2025 clashes.
“We cannot lend our sovereignty to anyone, even for a minute. It must remain with Thailand at all times,” Anutin said. He rejected the idea that Thailand could tolerate a small incursion on the assumption that it could reclaim the territory later.
Anutin spoke to reporters at 12.30 after presiding over the opening of the 2027 tactical air operations test and evaluation. He said cabinet ministers, MPs and senators involved in defence spending should see the armed forces’ capabilities for themselves. Economic and cyber conflict had taken on greater importance, he said, but conventional warfare remained a threat.
Asked whether the government would back the purchase of Gripen fighter jets, Anutin said he was ready to support measures that strengthened Thailand’s security. He said spending proposals were assessed for necessity and urged the public to consider the costs that border communities faced when fighting broke out.

“Ask the villagers who were affected, who had to evacuate,” he said, citing Kantharalak district in Si Sa Ket province, as well as communities in Surin and Buri Ram. Even if the government spent nothing on weapons, he said, it would still have to pay for evacuations, compensation and repairs when homes and property were damaged.
Anutin said the government and the armed forces shared responsibility for protecting Thai territory, civilians and military personnel. Frequent meetings between national leaders offered no guarantee against clashes, he said, and Thailand also had to prepare for terrorism and threats involving technology.
He said Thailand had no intention of invading another country and declined to speculate on how its military would fare against any particular opponent.
“If anyone thinks of invading or threatening us, we will not accept it,” he said. “Anyone who thinks of doing so will find us ready, and we will become more prepared.”

ตาก.title: Liverpool and adidas launch Thai-inspired collection worldwide
ตาก.summary:
Liverpool FC and adidas have launched Gold Leaf, a limited-edition lifestyle collection inspired by Thai gilding and dedicated to the club’s supporters in Thailand. The black-and-gold jersey at the centre of the range carries the word “Liverpool” in Thai script just below the back collar.
Liverpool said on its website that this is the first time adidas has chosen Thailand as the inspiration for a special Liverpool range sold worldwide.

The collection takes its name from the Thai practice of pressing thin sheets of gold leaf onto Buddha images as an act of devotion. Liverpool said the designs draw on the tradition’s associations with faith, respect and good fortune to express Thai supporters’ loyalty and their good wishes for the team.
On the jersey, the club’s name appears in deep red alongside a gold leaf motif. The front features a subtle diamond pattern, with a gold Liver Bird and adidas Originals Trefoil on the chest and matching trim around the V-neck.
Thai lettering also appears on the back of a T-shirt and track top, where a circular design pairs the club’s Thai and English names. The range includes track pants, shorts and a special edition of the adidas Originals Samba. The black leather trainers have red stripes and a fold-over tongue bearing a gold Liver Bird and the initials “LFC”.

Liverpool estimates it has more than 16 million supporters in Thailand, making it the country’s most-supported Premier League club. For the 2025–26 season, the club reported a cumulative television audience of 3.4 million in Thailand and 10.4 million followers across its social media channels in the country.
Liverpool made their sixth visit to Thailand in July 2015, when they opened their pre-season tour in Bangkok with a 4–0 win over a Thai All-Stars side.

ตาก.title: DSI probes smuggling of 10,000 tonnes of industrial waste
ตาก.summary:
Investigators say hazardous material shipped by sea to Chon Buri and transported to Rayong

The Department of Special Investigation has taken charge of a case involving at least 10,000 tonnes of industrial waste alleged to have been smuggled to eastern provinces in Thailand by Rayong Industrial Co.

The company is suspected of smuggling hazardous substances into Rayong and Chon Buri in the East as well as other provinces, the DSI said on Thursday.

DSI director-general Piya Raksakul approved the investigation on Nov 19, it added.

Thailand banned the import of electronic waste in September 2020 and further tightened regulations in 2025, but illegal disposal of large volumes of hazardous waste remains a serious health and pollution problem.

According to the DSI, officials found 15 buildings containing at least 10,000 tonnes of smuggled hazardous waste at the 153,600-square-metre compound of Rayong Industrial Co in Nikhom Phatthana district.

They also found video recordings of container trucks carrying banned hazardous substances that had been transported by sea to Laem Chabang port in Chon Buri. Further inspection showed the materials contained antimony, cadmium, lead and selenium.

Heavy metal contamination was also detected in nearby Prachin Buri province on Wednesday, when officials raided two recycling plants and found at least 500 tonnes of industrial waste in Sri Maha Phot district.

The Pollution Control Department said antimony, cadmium and lead were found along with oil-stained aluminium dust, aluminium scrap and stainless steel at Thai Rung Ruangkit Co.

At LD Metal (Thailand) Co, a search found antimony, lead, cadmium and selenium in electrical wire coatings that had been ground up and buried in its compound.

Forestry officials are also checking whether the latter site encroached on reserved forest land.

Officials unearth ground electrical wire coatings at a recycling plant in Prachin Buri on Wednesday. (Photo: Pollution Control Department)
